- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% in subsequent 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong bearish momentum, model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model exhibits strong lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative mid-period; adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to align with sentiment trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce noise and avoid overreaction to short-term sentiment spikes.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model tends to err on the side of bullish; force a 1–2% downward adjustment to reflect lack of conviction.
